paper_title: A SQUID-based microwave cavity search for dark-matter axions
notes: ADMX SQUID run (Asztalos et al.). Headline result = Fig.5, |g_agamma| excluded at 90% CL for local DM density 0.45 GeV/cm^3, masses ~3.34-3.54 ueV (paper quotes 3.3-3.53 ueV; plot frame 811.7-861.7 MHz). Fig.5 shows two limits from the medium-resolution channel assuming two line shapes: a completely virialized halo (broad ~kHz peak) and an unvirialized/cold-flow model (narrow peak, higher SNR). I report the VIRIALIZED (standard Maxwellian halo) limit, which the paper presents as the primary analysis ("optimized to search for the fully virialized axion signal"; the narrow-line/high-res channel was not used here). The virialized curve is the outer (weaker, higher-g) staircase, median ~2e-15 GeV^-1, range ~1.4-4.5e-15 (4.5e-15 spike is a real single mode-crossing step). The unvirialized limit sits ~1.3e-15 at the KSVZ line (factor ~1.6 below virialized, so within a factor of 2 of the reported curve either way). Curve extracted from the vector figure coupling_limits.eps in the arXiv e-print: coupling axis calibrated from log decade major ticks (10^-16..10^-10, 52.83 px/decade), mass axis from top-axis major ticks (3.35/3.40/3.45/3.50 ueV). No density rescaling applied.
